name: demo-erp
description: What the ERP promises its subscribers: the routes it serves, the shapes it accepts, and the events it publishes. The Commerce integration vendors this file and its tests fail when the two disagree.

import.partnersNote: version 3: the ERP holds no Commerce id (no commerceCompanyId, customerGroupId, emailDomain or website); which Commerce company is which customer is the integration's key map. version 5: websiteAccountClosed is Commerce's company Active/Blocked switch, stored as the ERP's read-only website account; it never changes the ERP's own credit block (blocking), which only the ERP sets. Either one stops an order. An import from an integration built before version 5 sends the same switch as blocked, read the same way
import.stockNote: quantities per warehouse for products the ERP already has (the integration sends a product's quantity at every source on Commerce's product and stock item events); a SKU the ERP does not have is reported under stock.unknown and not created; a stock-only import does not move lastImportAt

quote.contractNote: version 6: contractNumber names the contract whose line priced this one, or is null. A customer's contract lines in force for a SKU take the place of its loose contract prices and discounts for that SKU; the maximum discount still bounds the result

contracts.note: version 6: a contract is one customer's price agreement (number, partnerId, description, startingDate, endingDate, status draft | active | inactive, lines). Only an active contract between its starting and ending dates (both included) prices anything. Prices in force are its lines; when two contracts price one SKU at one minimum quantity for a customer, the later starting date wins, then the higher contract number
contracts.inForceNote: GET contracts/in-force answers today's prices in force for every customer with at least one line; with ?partnerId= it answers exactly that customer, lines possibly empty

fromCommerce.note: A move made IN Commerce carries origin: { event, eventId? }. The ERP records it, journals it as received, and raises no outbound event for it, so Commerce is not asked to do it twice.

be-observer.sales_order_shipment_create.note: items are THAT shipment's quantities, not the whole order; stockSourceCode names the warehouse it shipped from, or is null

be-observer.sales_order_hold.note: held true puts the Commerce order On Hold (the ERP created the order and held it for credit), false takes it off (a release); reason is the ERP's credit reason, or null on a release. A reject is a cancel and travels as sales_order_cancel

be-observer.sales_order_cancel.note: reason is one of the ERP's own cancellation reasons, for the Commerce order comment

be-observer.company_contract_update.note: version 6: raised whenever a change to a contract moves a customer's prices in force today. lines is that customer's whole set (contracts.priceLine or contracts.discountLine each), so a replay is harmless; an empty list means no contract price is left. A contract starting or ending with the calendar raises nothing: read GET contracts/in-force to follow dates

delivery.erpId: version 4: every delivered event's value carries erpId, the id the integration's ERP list gives this ERP (set at deploy as ERP_ID), when the ERP was deployed with one. An event without erpId is the single ERP's. The integration matches an order message to that ERP's part and a customer message to that ERP's key-map pairs
